ex_en: I have something I want to tell you.
note: pl. حاجات 7ājāt (حوايج 7wāyij means clothes/stuff). Very frequent filler word.

ex_en: I have a problem at work.
We have to find a solution to this matter.
I have a good idea.
What's your opinion of the house?
This is a chance that won't come again.

phrases.en: nice to meet you (lit. happy occasion)

ex_en: My luck isn't good today.
By God, you're lucky!
Tell me the truth.
That's a big lie.
note: pl. كذبات kidhbāt; كذب kidhb = lying (in general)

ex_en: What's the reason?
Forgive me, it was a mistake.
What's the difference between them?
What's the point of this talk?
note: pl. فوايد fawāyid; also 'interest' at a bank

ex_en: I have a habit of drinking coffee in the morning.
His condition has improved a bit.
The situation in the country is calm.
I want to talk with you about a matter.
The case is in court now.
Did you hear the news?
note: pl. أخبار akhbār (also 'the news' on TV)

ex_en: Tell me the story from the start.
I read a nice story.
This is a secret, don't tell anyone.

ex_ar: عندي ذكريات حلوة في الحوش هذا.
ex_en: I have sweet memories in this house.
I had a strange dream last night.
One must respect the elders.
note: Libyans also say قدر gadr for respect/esteem.

ex_en: Honour is a big thing for Libyans.

phrases.en: pleased to meet you (lit. we are honoured)

ex_en: Everyone has the freedom to choose.
We want peace in the country.
Safety is the most important thing.
Security has returned to the city.
He put a big effort into the work.
Life is hard these days.
The world has changed.
note: Also used for weather: الدنيا سخونة = it's hot.

ex_en: Living is expensive these days.
What's the meaning of this word?
This is your right.
I did it for your sake.
note: pl. خواطر khwāTir. على خاطر = because.

ex_en: His intention is good.

phrases.en: as you intend; you'll get what you intend

ex_en: This thing has no value.
This matter is very important.
I think about the children's future.
Leave the past in the past.
It was a tough experience.
He has ten years of experience.
Failure isn't the end of the world.
A disaster happened in the neighbourhood.
The flood was a catastrophe.
Everything is fate and destiny.
note: Used a lot about marriage. pl. أنصبة anSiba.

ex_en: This is God's apportioning.

ex_ar: هذا مكتوب، ما فيش هروب منه.
ex_tr: hādha maktūb, ma fīsh hrūb minnah.
ex_en: It's written; there's no escaping it.
We believe in divine decree and destiny.
note: Not to be confused with قدر gidir (cooking pot).

ex_en: I have doubts about what he says.
I don't trust him.
Dignity before everything.
How embarrassing! What did you do?
This is a disgrace in front of people.
He has a good reputation in the market.
I want a bit of rest.
Too much jealousy ruins things.
I long for home a lot.
Missing people is hard.
She doesn't speak out of shyness.
I'm only asking out of curiosity.
He has big ambitions.

phrases.en: my ambition is to finish my studies

ex_en: What's your goal in life?
note: pl. أهداف ahdāf. For football goal Libyans say قول gōl.

ex_en: What's our plan?
Teach me the method.
Which type do you want?
Part of the money was lost.
note: pl. أجزاء ajzā'. Also one of the 30 parts of the Quran.

phrases.en: the last part of the Quran

ex_en: Give me an example.
Now it's your turn.
I'm in difficult circumstances.
note: pl. ظروف DHurūf (mostly used in plural). Also 'envelope'.

ex_en: This is your responsibility.
The road is dangerous at night.
Everyone looks after his own interest.
Our relationship is good.

phrases.en: how are you related to him?
it's nothing to do with me

ex_en: What's my fault?
You have no excuse.
There's a blessing in this house.
They built a new mosque in the neighbourhood.
note: pl. مساجد masājid. Everyday word is جامع jāmi3.

ex_en: The imam has a beautiful voice.
I do my ablutions and pray.
note: Usually said with دار (to do) or توضى (to perform ablution).

phrases.en: are you in a state of ablution?

ex_en: We paid the zakat on the money.
I gave the fitra alms before the Eid prayer.
note: Libyans often call zakat al-fitr simply الفطرة.

ex_en: My mother went for umrah in Ramadan.
After iftar we go to tarawih prayers.
note: Plural form; singular ترويحة is rare.

ex_en: Today's sermon was long.
note: pl. خطب khuTab. Do not confuse with خطوبة (engagement).

ex_en: My grandfather always has prayer beads in his hand.
note: pl. سبح sibe7; also مسبحة misb7a

phrases.en: he counts praises on the beads

ex_en: The pilgrims circle the Kaaba.

ex_ar: نبي نمشي لمكة قبل ما نموت.
ex_tr: nibbi nimshi l-makka gbal ma nmūt.
ex_en: I want to go to Mecca before I die.
Which way is the qibla here?
The dawn prayer is two rak'as.
I prayed the obligatory prayer on time.
Giving charity is a Sunna.
Ramadan is a month of worship.
The door of repentance is open.
May God reward you.
A good deed is rewarded tenfold.

phrases.en: do it as a good deed

ex_en: There's great reward in it.
This is something forbidden.
note: Exists in the deck as an exclamation; this card is the noun sense.

ex_en: Pray istikhara before you decide.
She went to the sheikh to recite healing verses over her.
note: Common practice in Libya against envy and evil eye.

ex_en: Put the Quran copy on top of the shelf.
He memorised a new sura today.
He recited the Throne Verse.
note: pl. آيات āyāt. Also 'a marvel': آية في الجمال.

en: al-Fatiha; recitation to seal an agreement
ex_en: We recited al-Fatiha for his soul.
note: In Libya reciting the Fatiha also seals an engagement.

ex_en: There's a hadith that says so.
Pray for the Prophet (calm down).
note: pl. أنبياء anbiyā. 'صلي على النبي' is said to calm someone.

ex_en: The Messenger of God said…
His faith is strong.
May God have mercy on his soul.
note: pl. أرواح arwā7. Also 'self': روحي = myself.

ex_en: May God admit you to paradise.
It's hell in the summer.
We work for this world and the hereafter.
Am I to wait for you till Judgment Day?

phrases.en: signs of the end of days

ex_en: He's sleeping like an angel.
note: pl. ملايكة malāyka. Not ملك malik (king).

ex_en: I seek refuge in God from Satan.
note: pl. شياطين shayāTīn. Also a naughty child.

ex_en: My grandmother tells us stories about the jinn.
This is from envy (the evil eye).
note: Libyans say ما شاء الله to ward it off; also called العين.

ex_en: She burned incense in the house.
note: Burned at weddings, Fridays and against the evil eye.

ex_en: May God have mercy on the martyrs.
The funeral is after the afternoon prayer.
We visited my grandfather's grave.
Did they see the crescent? Is Eid tomorrow?
note: The sighting of the crescent decides when Ramadan and Eid begin.

ex_ar: ليلة القدر الناس الكل في الجوامع.
ex_tr: lēlat il-qadr in-nās il-kull fi l-jwāmi3.
ex_en: On the Night of Power everyone is at the mosques.
note: In Libya kids often get new clothes and girls get henna on the 27th.

phrases.en: prayer on the Night of Power

ex_en: On Ashura they make dried meat dishes.
note: Libyans cook dishes with قديد (cured meat) from Eid al-Adha.

ex_en: Imsak is at half past four.
Fasting in summer is hard.
note: Same meaning as صوم; صيام is more common in religious talk.

phrases.en: the six days of Shawwal fast

ex_en: Libyan hospitality is famous.
Generosity is one of our customs.

en: invitation to a meal; dinner party
ex_ar: عندنا عزومة الليلة في حوش خالي.
ex_en: We have a dinner invitation tonight at my uncle's.
He held a big banquet for the wedding.

phrases.en: he slaughtered and held a feast

ex_en: On Friday we have a picnic at the beach.
note: Libyan/Maghrebi word for a festive outing with a big meal.

ex_en: I brought you a gift on the occasion of your success.
This is a gift for you.
We had visitors yesterday.
Thanks for the invitation.
note: pl. دعوات da3wāt. دعوة أمي = my mother's blessing/prayer.

ex_en: Your friend sends you greetings.
Their engagement is next week.

ex_ar: الملاك يوم الخميس والعرس بعد شهر.
ex_tr: il-mlāk yōm il-khmīs w-il-3ers ba3d shahr.
ex_en: The marriage contract is Thursday and the wedding a month later.
note: Libyan word for the signing of the marriage contract (عقد القران).

ex_en: Dowries are expensive these days.

ex_ar: العروسة قاعدة تشري في الجهاز متاعها.
ex_tr: il-3arūsa gā3da tishri fi j-jhāz mtā3ha.
ex_en: The bride is buying her trousseau.
She put henna on her hands for Eid.
The old ladies let out ululations.
We preserve our traditions.
Malouf is part of our heritage.
Libyan culture is a mix.
The Libyan dialect has Italian words.
As the proverb says…
note: pl. أمثال amthāl. Not مثل mithl (like).

ex_en: He told us a funny joke.
My grandfather has great wisdom.
He loves folk poetry.
His uncle is a well-known poet.
He said it as a ghnawat 3alam.
note: Bedouin genre (غناوة العلم): a one-line sung poem of love or longing.

phrases.en: he knows lots of ghnawa lines

ex_en: At the wedding they played marskawi.
note: Popular Libyan wedding music genre, originally from the east/south.

ex_en: He loves art and drawing.
He's a well-known artist in Libya.
note: pl. فنانين fannānīn; in Libya often means a singer.

ex_en: We hung a painting in the living room.
note: pl. لوحات lō7āt. Also number plate (لوحة السيارة).

ex_ar: في العرس فيه رقص لنص الليل.
ex_tr: fi l-3ers fīh rugS l-nuSS il-lēl.
ex_en: At the wedding there's dancing till midnight.
Did you hear the drum? There's a wedding.
He knows how to play the darbuka.
My uncle plays the oud.
They brought a band for the wedding.
There's a festival in the Old City.
We went to the book fair.
Leptis Magna has Roman ruins.
Libya has ancient civilizations.
One moment, I'm coming now.
I haven't seen her for a while.
note: pl. فترات fatrāt. Also a work shift: الفترة الصباحية.

phrases.en: a while ago; for a while

ex_en: How long is the contract?
This house is a century old.
note: pl. قرون grūn. Also 'horn' of an animal.

ex_en: Nothing has changed for a decade.
note: Formal; in speech Libyans usually say عشر سنين. Also 'contract' and 'necklace'.

phrases.en: ten years (common way to say it)

ex_ar: في زمن جدي ما فيش كهربا.
ex_tr: fi zaman jiddi ma fīsh kahraba.
ex_en: In my grandfather's time there was no electricity.
We're in the age of technology.
note: pl. عصور 3uSūr. Same word as العصر (afternoon prayer).

ex_en: The holiday is a whole week.
note: pl. أسابيع asābī3. Everyday Libyan is جمعة jum3a.

ex_en: What are you planning for the weekend?
note: English loan; the Libyan weekend is Friday–Saturday.

ex_en: I told you from the beginning.
The end of the film was sad.
He came exactly on time.
He gave me a week's grace.
I'll come to you in late morning.
At New Year the streets are empty.
What's today's date in the Hijri month?
Is my birthday by the Gregorian or Hijri calendar?
He hung the new calendar in the kitchen.
Winter time has started.
What do you do in your free time?

ex_ar: راس العام الهجري في أول محرم.
ex_tr: rās il-3ām il-hijri fi awwil mu7arram.
ex_en: Islamic New Year is on 1 Muharram.
The umrah is in Rajab.
It's mid-Sha'ban and people are preparing for Ramadan.
I fast the six days of Shawwal.

ex_ar: العيد الكبير في عشرة ذو الحجة.
ex_en: Eid al-Adha is on 10 Dhu al-Hijja.

phrases.en: the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja

ex_en: The house is twenty metres long.
Add two centimetres.
The distance is a hundred kilometres.
note: Often shortened to كيلو in speech.

ex_en: Two hundred grams of olives.
The lorry is carrying ten tons.
Give me half a kilo of tomatoes.
It's forty degrees today.
What size do you want?
How tall are you?
note: Also used as adverb على طول (straight on).

ex_en: The door is a metre wide.
How deep is the sea here?
There's a rise in prices.
The plot's area is five hundred metres.
What's the distance from Tripoli to Misrata?
This amount isn't enough.
The number of people was large.
note: pl. أعداد a3dād. For a phone/house number Libyans say نمرة or رقم.

ex_en: The average salary is low.
What's the total?
Give me a piece of the cake.
note: pl. قطع giTa3. قطعة أرض = a plot of land.

ex_en: The price has doubled.
note: pl. أضعاف aD3āf. ضعف Da3f means weakness.

ex_en: It didn't move even an inch.
We bought a sack of flour.
note: pl. شوالات shwālāt. Same letters as the month شوال.

ex_en: It doesn't look good.
The table is square-shaped.
note: pl. مربعات murabba3āt. Also adj.: متر مربع.

ex_en: Draw a circle.
The sweets are cut into triangles.
The house is rectangular.
His handwriting can't be read.
note: pl. خطوط khTūT. Also phone line / SIM.

ex_en: This is an important point.
note: pl. نقاط nugāT / نقط nugaT. Also checkpoint: نقطة تفتيش.

phrases.en: drop by drop; point by point

ex_en: The zawiya teaches children the Quran.
note: pl. زوايا zwāya. Sufi lodges (e.g. زاوية سيدي عبد السلام) are important in Libya.

ex_en: The price is three hundred dinars.
The salary is a little over four hundred.
I gave him five hundred dinars.
The car has done six hundred thousand kilometres.
The rent is seven hundred a month.

phrases.en: seven hundred and fifty (lit. and a half)

ex_en: The mobile costs eight hundred.
Nine hundred ninety-nine.
The salary is three thousand.
The car is ten thousand.
The house is a hundred thousand dinars.
The budget is in the billions.
Thousands of people came to the match.
Hundreds of cars are parked.
note: Plural of مية. Also ميات miyyāt in speech.

ex_en: I've told you dozens of times.
Take your fifth.
He hasn't finished even a tenth of the work.
note: pl. أعشار a3shār; also decimal places.

ex_en: Two and four are even numbers.
Cars with odd numbers drive today.
I gave him my vote.
note: pl. أصوات aSwāt. Same word as 'voice/sound'.

ex_en: Libya is still waiting for a constitution.
note: pl. دساتير dasātīr. 'دستور!' is also an old expression asking permission to enter.

ex_en: There's a petrol shortage these days.
note: pl. أزمات azamāt. Libyans speak of أزمة السيولة, أزمة الكهربا, etc.

ex_en: I don't like talking politics.
Libya is our homeland.

ex_ar: من بعد الثورة تغيرت حاجات هلبة.
ex_en: After the revolution many things changed.
May God keep war away from us.
Parliament didn't approve the law.
We sat in the guest room with the guests.
note: pl. مجالس majālis. Also council: المجلس البلدي.

ex_en: Everyone talks about democracy.
We want justice for all people.
God is just.
note: Libyans also say عدل to mean 'fair, even'.

phrases.en: justice is the basis of rule

ex_en: This is unfair!
Corruption is everywhere.
High prices are breaking people's backs.
Poverty has increased in the country.
Unemployment is high among young people.
There has to be order in the house.
He has great authority.
note: pl. سلطات sulTāt. Not سلاطة salāTa (salad).

ex_en: That was the agreement between us.
There's a demonstration in the square.

ex_ar: عيد الاستقلال في أربعة وعشرين ديسمبر.
ex_en: Independence Day is on 24 December.
He works at the oil corporation.
I worked with an international organisation.
The budget isn't enough.
Services in the neighbourhood are poor.

ex_ar: السلاح لازم يكون عند الدولة بس.
ex_en: Weapons should only be in the state's hands.
They made a truce.
There was a reconciliation between the two families.
note: Often done by elders (أعيان) in Libya.

ex_en: Loneliness is hard for old people.
The media don't tell everything.
Happiness is in little things.
note: Also a title: سعادة السفير (His Excellency).

ex_en: I have no appetite to eat.
note: pl. نفوس nfūs. Also 'same' (نفس الحاجة) and نفس nafas (breath).

ex_en: Use your head!
He has no conscience.
note: pl. ضماير Damāyir. Also 'pronoun' in grammar.

ex_en: May God reward you with good.
note: Common in greetings: صباح الخير, خير؟ (what's wrong?).

phrases.en: he's a good person; it's plenty

ex_en: May God keep evil away from us.
note: Libyans say بعيد الشر (far be it!) when someone mentions illness.

ex_en: Honesty saves you.
This is entrusted to you.

phrases.en: please, I beg you (lit. a trust on you)

ex_en: This is betrayal.
The dog is a symbol of loyalty.
May God send down mercy on him.
I don't want pity from anyone.
A mother's tenderness can't be replaced.
There's great affection between us.
Our friendship goes back to school days.
note: Libyan everyday word; صداقة Sadāga is more formal.

ex_en: There's no enmity between us at all.
I have a feeling he'll come.
It's a lovely feeling when you return home.

ex_ar: أني في حيرة، ما نعرفش شن ندير.
ex_tr: āni fi 7īra, ma na3rafsh shin ndīr.
ex_en: I'm torn, I don't know what to do.
Regret is no use now.
We were bored to death.
note: Libyans also say قلق galag for boredom.

ex_en: That's all in your imagination.
His mentality is old-fashioned.
He has a calm nature.
note: pl. طباع Tbā3. طبعاً = of course.

ex_en: A man of good character.
Speak politely.
His behaviour has changed.
This is a trick to get money.
note: pl. حيل 7iyal. ما في اليد حيلة = there's nothing one can do.

ex_en: I have a surprise for you.
We met by chance.
note: pl. صدف Sudaf. Same spelling as صدفة Sadafa (seashell).

ex_en: I want to give you some advice.
I have one condition.
The choice is yours.
He wants to continue his studies.
He has no interest in studying.
It caught my attention.
I have a small remark.
That's a promise from me.
He swore an oath.
note: Same word as 'right (side)'. pl. أيمان aymān.

ex_ar: الحوش هذا عنده ميزة، قريب من البحر.
ex_tr: il-7ōsh hādha 3indah mīza, grīb min il-ba7r.
ex_en: This house has an advantage: it's near the sea.
There's a shortage of medicine.
I want a change in my life.
There's progress in the work.
Your son is progressing in his studies.
His level is high.
The work is very stressful.
note: ضغط الدم = blood pressure (already in deck).

ex_en: He's very strong.
He has weak eyesight.
I want a bit of quiet.
The house is a mess!
He's originally from Gharyan.
Self-respect is a big thing.
What you say is right.
Respect people's feelings.
He worked enthusiastically.
It takes courage.
Laziness stopped him finishing.
He's too conceited.
A great man is known by his humility.
The beauty of the sea in summer.
note: Also a boys' name. Not جمال jammāl (camel driver).

ex_en: I have an important piece of information.
Our fate is in God's hands.
My wish is to see my mother comfortable.
Watch out!
note: In many phrases: ردّ بالك (be careful), على بالي (I thought).

phrases.en: I thought; it crossed my mind

ex_en: He worked carefully.
We bought the sacrificial sheep early this year.
note: pl. أضاحي aDā7i. Usually a ram (كبش / علوش).

phrases.en: the price of the Eid sheep

ex_en: They slaughtered an animal for the guests.

ex_ar: بوطبيلة يدور في الحومة قبل الفجر.
ex_tr: būTbēla ydūr fi l-7ōma gbal il-fajr.
ex_en: The suhoor drummer goes round the neighbourhood before dawn.
note: Libyan name for the مسحراتي; kids give him money at the end of Ramadan.

ex_en: We hear the takbir on Eid morning.
note: تكبيرات العيد are chanted before the Eid prayer.

ex_en: They held a full Quran recitation for their grandfather's soul.
note: Often read at funerals and on special occasions.

ex_en: He asked the sheikh for a ruling.
I have a vow to fast three days.
He owes expiation for a broken oath.
note: Also said after a minor misfortune: كفارة! (may it be expiation for your sins).

phrases.en: may it atone for your sins (to someone hurt)

ex_en: We went to the market to buy the Eid clothes.
note: Children get new clothes for Eid al-Fitr.

ex_ar: صلاة العيد في الساحة الساعة سبعة.
ex_tr: Salāt il-3īd fi s-sā7a s-sā3a sab3a.
ex_en: The Eid prayer is in the square at seven.
note: Held outdoors in a مصلى on Eid morning.

ex_en: Let's meet after the Friday prayer.
note: The main communal prayer; shops close around it.

ex_ar: قعدة الشاهي مع الصحاب ما تتعوضش.
ex_tr: g3adat ish-shāhi ma3a S-S7āb ma tit3awwaDsh.
ex_en: Tea get-togethers with friends are irreplaceable.
note: pl. قعدات g3adāt. Central to Libyan social life.

ex_en: That's not flattery, it's the truth.

ex_ar: مشينا لواجب العزا في حوش جارنا.
ex_en: We went to pay condolences at our neighbour's house.
note: Mourning lasts three days with visitors received at home or in a tent (خيمة).

ex_en: There's a prayer room at work.
